newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid sees $25 million Sterling charge.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid sees $25 million Sterling charge.

text.p: Polaroid Corp. said Wednesday it expected to take a $25 million charge in the fourth quarter as part of a sales, marketing and development deal with Sterling Dry Imaging Systems Inc.

The company said it completed previously announced agreements with Sterling, for the sale of some assets and for product development cooperation, but it expected to take a charge for severence, inventory, fixed-asset write-offs and other costs.
Polaroid had initially said it would take a charge of between $15 million and $20 million due to the Sterling deal.
Polaroid also said it would take an additional $15 million pre-tax charge in the fourth quarter to write-down parts and capital equipment for a printer project and other costs.
The company said it had shifted its strategy for the development of desktop priners for the home and office market to emphasise alliances with leading printer manufacturers.

Under the Sterling deal, Sterling Dry Imaging, a unit of Sterling Diagnostic Imaging Inc., acquired Polaroid's assets relating to the hardware manufacturing, worldwide marketing, sales and servicing of the Helios Laser Imaging system.
Sterling also contracted Polaroid to develop new medical diagnostic imaging technologies and products to supply it with Helios medical diagnostic imaging film, the company said.
